title: Synthetic alert bucketing and routing grooming notes
content:
Context and goal:
- Problem: we increasingly rely on synthetic signals (health checks, synthetic queries, smoke tests) and user-facing SLOs. Current alerting UX lumps these in with customer-facing incidents and creates noise for oncall. Need a UX and routing model that treats synthetic signals as first-class, with configurable bucketing, channel routing, and tenant-level overrides.

Notes from 2024-11-05 kickoff:
- Primary objective: let teams define alert buckets (severity-like) derived from SLO/metric thresholds and synthetic signal classes, then map buckets to channel routing policies with calendar-aware quiet hours and duty-roster rules.
- Secondary: enable safe defaults at org/tenant level and easy per-service overrides (copyable templates).
- Constraints: must integrate with existing notification fabric (email, slack, pagerduty, webhook) and keep template/per-route cost telemetry visible in Console.

User stories (prioritized):
1) As an SRE, I want to create a synthetic check type (e.g., latency-smoke-10s) and assign it to a "pre-incident" bucket so that only oncall is paged after repeated failures.
2) As a product owner, I want tenant-wide defaults that guard rails teams can opt into so we avoid paging for low-value flakes.
3) As an incident commander, I want to escalate automatically from slack thread -> pager when aggregated error rate exceeds bucket threshold.
4) As a platform admin, I want to see per-bucket cost and downstream chatter (number of notifications per channel) over time.

Proposed model (conceptual):
- Signal category: synthetic | production | user-reported. (Selectable tag per monitor)
- Buckets: reduce to 3 canonical buckets for UX simplicity: info (log), warning (email/slack), urgent (pager). Each bucket has:
  - evaluation window (n minutes),
  - repetition count (e.g., 3 fails within window),
  - debounce/auto-suppress rules (duration),
  - ticket template binding (optionally create a ticket in linked tracker).
- Routing policies: map buckets to ordered channel lists with optional per-channel throttles and escalation delays. Example:
  - urgent -> PagerDuty primary -> Slack #ops (notify) -> Email (digest)
  - warning -> Slack #service-alerts -> Email digest
  - info -> Email digest only
- Quiet-hours & calendar-awareness: policies accept org-level quiet-hours with overrides by team and service. Quiet-hours become "delayed routing" not "dropped".

Wireframe notes (rough, for 3 canvas panels in Console):
Panel A: Monitor config header
- Fields: name, signal category (dropdown), owner (team selector), linked SLOs (multi-select)
- Small inline CTA: "Assign to bucket" (dropdown) + quick preview of routing icons (pager, slack, email, webhook)

Panel B: Bucket editor (cards)
- Cards for Info / Warning / Urgent (left-to-right)
- Card contents: toggle active, evaluation window, repetition, suppression duration, sample noise-reduction checklist (ignore-on-deploy, ignore-known-issue-tags)
- Inline "test trigger" button: simulates a signal and shows expected channels and message payload sample.

Panel C: Routing & schedule canvas
- Drag-and-drop channel ordering for each bucket; per-channel settings open in right-hand pane: escalation delay, channel-level throttle (max per hour), message template (markdown)
- Calendar overlay: highlight quiet-hours for channels that support it; link to org calendar to auto-detect on-call overrides
- Tenant override toggle: apply tenant-defaults or create service-level copy

Behavioral examples (edge cases):
- Flaky synthetic checks: default to "info" with a 5x repetition requirement and progressive escalation to avoid noisy pages.
- Multi-region degradation: if multiple monitors in different regions fire within 60s, escalate one shared bucket to urgent after cross-region aggregation.
- Dependabot-style automation alerts: route to webhook and email only.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Create and assign a monitor to a bucket, define repetition window and suppression duration.
- Map a bucket to at least two channels with an escalation delay.
- Test trigger shows exactly which channels will receive a message and sample payload.
- Tenant can set and lock a default routing policy; a service can copy and customize.
- Quiet-hours delay works: triggers during quiet-hours are queued and sent at end unless suppressed.

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs:
- How many buckets? Three keeps UX simple but some teams want finer granularity. If we expose an advanced mode, we need clearer naming.
- Aggregation rules for cross-region signals: do we require a separate "meta-monitor" to declare aggregation boundaries, or infer by monitor tags?
- Cost telemetry integration: what metrics are captured per-channel? messages_sent, pages_triggered, estimated_token-cost for message payloads? Need infra input.
- Should synthetic signals have their own "policy library" (templates tuned to low-value flakes) vs reusing production policies?

Implementation notes for eng teams:
- API contract: expose new "bucket" field on monitor objects and a routingPolicy object referencing channel IDs with ordering and throttle params. Keep backwards compatibility by defaulting monitors without bucket to existing routing.
- Frontend: three-column layout with a shared state model to preview simulated payload. Reuse existing channel-picker component.
- Backend: implement a lightweight queue for quiet-hours buffering with small TTL and idempotent delivery.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Ethan: draft API schema for monitor/bucket/routingPolicy (JIRA JIRA-OPS-10012) - ETA 2024-12-01
- Nora: mock high-fidelity frames for Panel B and C (Figma) - ETA 2024-11-20
- Samir: investigate cost telemetry feasibility and propose storage schema - ETA 2024-12-10
- Maya: compile tenant-default configuration proposals and propose RBAC model - ETA 2024-12-05

Meeting notes (2024-11-12 design sync):
- Consensus: start with 3 buckets, but allow advanced expansion via "custom buckets" in an admin mode.
- Decision to keep simulated "test trigger" in MVP after it proved useful for reducing configuration errors.
- Need to coordinate with SRE on aggregation rules for multi-region signals.

Misc / quick sketches:
- Sample message payload (for slack):
  - [ALERT] latency-smoke-10s (service-x)
  - bucket: warning | repetition: 3/5 | window: 10m
  - link: /app/service-x/monitor/latency-smoke-10s
  - actions: acknowledge | open runbook | silence for 30m

- UX copy candidates for routing policy save CTA:
  - "Save routing and notify" vs "Save policy (dry-run)" (prefer second option for safer rollout)

Notes-to-self: include example of tenant-lock for regulated customers where paging cannot be disabled at service level.

Next sync: 2024-11-19 10:00 PT (design + SRE).
